exposure: nasopharyngeal bacterial colonization (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae)
cohort: The study included 614 children who had experienced respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract infections, with an additional external validation cohort of 164 children.
finding: Peripheral blood eosinophil count, serum 25(OH)D and IgM levels, and nasopharyngeal bacterial colonization (specifically Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae) were significantly associated with recurrent wheezing following RSV infection, and a predictive model showed moderate-to-good diagnostic performance.
